author: Christian Jones
title: Trio of Wiregrass medalists reflect on their time at Special Olympics - NewsBreak
text:
By Christian Jones ,
2 hours ago
DOTHAN, Ala. ( WDHN )—The city of Dothan will now forever be known as the home to a trio of Olympic athletes whose hard work certainly paid off after Gabriella Baker, Andrew Neve, and Kayla Kelly brought home multiple medals in the 2026 Special Olympic USA Games.
For Baker, she put on a historic performance in Minnesota, showcasing her blazing speed in front of spectators and not only coming in first place but doing so convincingly.
Baker etched her name into the history books by setting the Special Olympics USA record for the fastest time in the 800-meter run, finishing just under 2 minutes and 34 seconds.
But winning medals comes naturally for Andrew Neve.
As someone who has already been crowned a world champion in volleyball, Neve showed up and showed out at the Special Olympics, winning bronze medals in the 50-yard freestyle and relay swimming races, then going on to win the 100-yard freestyle.
And Kayla Kelly brought back multiple bronze medals in bocce, an Italian lawn bowling game where players try to get a large ball as close as possible to a smaller target ball.
But Kelly’s medal has an extra-special meaning to it because she won it with her unified partner, her mother, Gina Kelly.
Each of the three athletes wanted to take a moment to thank all their coaches, the Doug Tew community, and the people of the Wiregrass for being with them every step of the way.
But they also hope that their achievements serve as proof that anything is possible for anyone, despite any kind of limitations.
For now, these Olympic athletes are enjoying their success while waiting to see whether they will be selected for the World Games in Chile, set to start next year.
